## Multidimensional Fourier Sine Series

### Setup

Let \(f:\mathbb{X}\to\mathbb{R}\) (or \(\mathbb{C}\)) with \(\mathbb{X}=[0,X_1]\times\cdots\times[0,X_D]\). The natural sine basis on \(\mathbb{X}\) is obtained by taking the tensor product of the one-dimensional sine bases on each factor. For each dimension \(d\) introduce the wavenumbers

\[
k_{n_d}^{(d)}=\frac{n_d\pi}{X_d},\qquad n_d=1,2,3,\dots
\]

and the corresponding normalized eigenfunctions of the Dirichlet Laplacian on \([0,X_d]\),

\[
\varphi_{n_d}^{(d)}(x_d)=\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{X_d}}\sin\!\Big(\tfrac{n_d\pi x_d}{X_d}\Big).
\]

A multi-index is \(\mathbf{n}=(n_1,\dots,n_D)\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}^{D}\). Define the product basis function

\[
\Phi_{\mathbf{n}}(\mathbf{x})=\prod_{d=1}^{D}\varphi_{n_d}^{(d)}(x_d)
=\prod_{d=1}^{D}\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{X_d}}\sin\!\Big(\tfrac{n_d\pi x_d}{X_d}\Big).
\]

These \(\{\Phi_{\mathbf{n}}\}_{\mathbf{n}\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}^{D}}\) form a complete orthonormal system in \(L^{2}(\mathbb{X})\) (with respect to the flat measure \(d\mathbf{x}=dx_1\cdots dx_D\)), since each one-dimensional sine system is complete in \(L^{2}([0,X_d])\) and tensor products of complete orthonormal systems are complete.

### General form

The **multidimensional Fourier sine series** of \(f\) is

\[
\boxed{\;
f(\mathbf{x})\sim\sum_{\mathbf{n}\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}^{D}}\widehat{f}_{\mathbf{n}}\,\Phi_{\mathbf{n}}(\mathbf{x})
=\sum_{n_1=1}^{\infty}\cdots\sum_{n_D=1}^{\infty}\widehat{f}_{\mathbf{n}}\,
\prod_{d=1}^{D}\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{X_d}}\sin\!\Big(\tfrac{n_d\pi x_d}{X_d}\Big),
\;}
\]

with the (orthonormal) sine coefficients

\[
\widehat{f}_{\mathbf{n}}
=\langle f,\Phi_{\mathbf{n}}\rangle_{L^{2}(\mathbb{X})}
=\int_{\mathbb{X}} f(\mathbf{x})\,\Phi_{\mathbf{n}}(\mathbf{x})\,d\mathbf{x}
=\Bigg(\prod_{d=1}^{D}\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{X_d}}\Bigg)
\int_{0}^{X_1}\!\!\cdots\!\!\int_{0}^{X_D}
f(\mathbf{x})\prod_{d=1}^{D}\sin\!\Big(\tfrac{n_d\pi x_d}{X_d}\Big)\,d\mathbf{x}.
\]

Equivalently, using the unnormalized convention (each factor carries a plain \(2/X_d\)),

\[
f(\mathbf{x})\sim\sum_{n_1,\dots,n_D\ge 1}
\Bigg(\prod_{d=1}^{D}\tfrac{2}{X_d}\Bigg)
\Bigg[\int_{\mathbb{X}} f(\mathbf{x})\prod_{d=1}^{D}\sin\!\Big(\tfrac{n_d\pi x_d}{X_d}\Big)\,d\mathbf{x}\Bigg]
\prod_{d=1}^{D}\sin\!\Big(\tfrac{n_d\pi x_d}{X_d}\Big).
\]

The coefficients factor as iterated one-dimensional sine transforms when \(f\) is separable; in general they do not factor, and the series is a genuine \(D\)-fold sum.

### Convergence conditions

Convergence is governed by the regularity of \(f\) and by the boundary behavior, because the sine basis enforces homogeneous Dirichlet data on the whole boundary \(\partial\mathbb{X}\).

**1. \(L^{2}\) convergence (Parseval).** If \(f\in L^{2}(\mathbb{X})\), then

\[
\sum_{\mathbf{n}}|\widehat{f}_{\mathbf{n}}|^{2}=\|f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{X})}^{2}<\infty,
\]

and the partial sums \(S_{N}(\mathbf{x})=\sum_{\max_d n_d\le N}\widehat{f}_{\mathbf{n}}\Phi_{\mathbf{n}}(\mathbf{x})\) converge to \(f\) in \(L^{2}(\mathbb{X})\). This is the Riesz–Fischer theorem applied to the complete orthonormal system \(\{\Phi_{\mathbf{n}}\}\).

**2. Pointwise / uniform convergence (regularity + boundary compatibility).** Sufficient conditions:

- If \(f\in C^{D+1}(\mathbb{X})\) (or, more sharply, \(f\) has square-integrable mixed partial derivatives up to order \(D\) in the Sobolev sense, i.e. \(f\in H^{1}_{0,\mathrm{mix}}\) with each first mixed partial in \(L^{2}\)), **and** \(f\) satisfies the **Dirichlet boundary compatibility**

\[
f(\mathbf{x})\big|_{x_d=0}=f(\mathbf{x})\big|_{x_d=X_d}=0\quad\text{for every }d=1,\dots,D
\]

(i.e. \(f\) vanishes on the entire boundary \(\partial\mathbb{X}\)), then the sine series converges **absolutely and uniformly** on \(\mathbb{X}\) to \(f\).

The boundary condition is essential: the sine basis functions all vanish on \(\partial\mathbb{X}\), so any uniform limit must also vanish there. If \(f\) does not vanish on the boundary, the series still converges in \(L^{2}\) and converges pointwise in the interior, but it exhibits the multidimensional analogue of the Gibbs phenomenon near boundary faces and cannot converge uniformly on \(\overline{\mathbb{X}}\).

- **Pointwise convergence in the interior.** If \(f\) is piecewise \(C^{1}\) on \(\mathbb{X}\), then at every interior point \(\mathbf{x}\in(0,X_1)\times\cdots\times(0,X_D)\) where \(f\) is continuous, the (rectangularly ordered) partial sums converge to \(f(\mathbf{x})\). At an interior point of jump discontinuity the series converges to the average of the one-sided limits along each coordinate direction (the multidimensional Gibbs value). This follows by iterating the one-dimensional Dirichlet–Jordan / Dini test in each coordinate.

**3. Sobolev / energy convergence.** If \(f\in H^{1}_{0}(\mathbb{X})\) (the closure of \(C^{\infty}_{c}(\mathbb{X})\) in the \(H^{1}\) norm, i.e. \(f\) and its first derivatives are square-integrable and \(f\) has zero trace on \(\partial\mathbb{X}\)), then

\[
\sum_{\mathbf{n}}\Big(\sum_{d=1}^{D}\big(\tfrac{n_d\pi}{X_d}\big)^{2}\Big)|\widehat{f}_{\mathbf{n}}|^{2}=\|\nabla f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{X})}^{2}<\infty,
\]

because \(\Phi_{\mathbf{n}}\) are the eigenfunctions of the Dirichlet Laplacian \(-\Delta\) with eigenvalues \(\lambda_{\mathbf{n}}=\sum_{d}(n_d\pi/X_d)^{2}\). The series then converges to \(f\) in the \(H^{1}_{0}\) energy norm. Higher Sobolev regularity \(f\in H^{s}_{0}(\mathbb{X})\) gives convergence in \(H^{s'}\) for every \(s'<s\).

### Summary statement

> The multidimensional Fourier sine series of \(f\) on \(\mathbb{X}=[0,X_1]\times\cdots\times[0,X_D]\) is the \(D\)-fold sum \(\sum_{\mathbf{n}\ge 1}\widehat{f}_{\mathbf{n}}\prod_{d}\sqrt{2/X_d}\sin(n_d\pi x_d/X_d)\), with coefficients given by the inner product of \(f\) against the product sine basis. It converges to \(f\) in \(L^{2}(\mathbb{X})\) for every \(f\in L^{2}(\mathbb{X})\); it converges pointwise to \(f\) at interior points of continuity under piecewise \(C^{1}\) regularity; and it converges absolutely and uniformly to \(f\) on \(\overline{\mathbb{X}}\) when \(f\) is sufficiently smooth (e.g. \(C^{D+1}\), or in the mixed Sobolev class with integrable mixed derivatives) **and** satisfies the homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition \(f|_{\partial\mathbb{X}}=0\). The boundary condition is necessary for uniform convergence because every basis function vanishes on \(\partial\mathbb{X}\).
